extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for requesting that a U.S. patent application be advanced out of turn (made “special”), and for requesting suspension/deferral of Office action; includes grounds, documentary requirements, fees, and prosecution procedures (including accelerated examination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancement of examination (37 CFR 1.102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will not be advanced out of turn for examination or further action except as provided by this part, upon order of the Commissioner to expedite Office business, upon a request under 1.102(b), or upon filing of a petition under 1.102(c) or (d) with a showing justifying advancing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the baseline: new applications are ordinarily taken up in effective filing date order; only specified orders/requests/petitions or Commissioner action will advance an application out of turn. Petitions must make a showing that, in the Commissioner’s opinion, justifies advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of special cases advanced out of turn
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated categories of applications that are considered 'special' and may be advanced out of turn (examples include: applications made special by departmental request, applications made special by petition, reissue applications in stayed litigation, applications remanded by an appellate tribunal, applications treated as special when taken up by an examiner by effective filing date, applications appearing to interfere, applications ready for allowance, applications in condition for final rejection, pending more than 5 years, reexamination proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This list identifies categories that receive priority. When an application falls within one of these categories it should be advanced by examiners/units accordingly; see MPEP cross-references (e.g., §§ 707.02, 714.13, 1207, 1309).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective manufacture petition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To make an application special on the ground of prospective manufacture, petitioner must file the petition with the fee (37 CFR 1.17(h)) and a statement alleging possession of sufficient capital and facilities (approximate amounts/nature), or that sufficient capital/facilities will be made available, plus corroboration if the prospective manufacturer is an individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional required allegations: (B) that the prospective manufacturer will not manufacture or increase manufacture unless certain that the patent will be granted; (C) an obligation to manufacture in the U.S. or possessions immediately upon allowance; (D) that a careful/prior-art search was made or good knowledge exists. Applicant must provide one copy of each reference deemed most closely related if not already of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual infringement petition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be made special because of actual infringement (not prospective) upon payment of the fee and filing a petition with a statement alleging (A) an infringing device/product or method actually on the market/in use; (B) a rigid comparison showing some claims are unquestionably infringed; and (C) that a careful/prior-art search was made or good knowledge of pertinent prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must provide copies of the most closely related references if not of record. Models/specimens of the infringing product should not be submitted unless requested. The petition is subject to further showing as needed by the facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's health petition
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be made special on the basis of applicant's health upon filing a petition accompanied by evidence (e.g., a doctor's or other medical certificate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fee is required for a petition based on age or health (37 CFR 1.102(c)). The evidence should show the state of health such that the applicant might not be available to assist in prosecution if the application ran its normal course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's age petition
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be made special if the applicant is 65 years of age or older upon filing a petition including evidence (e.g., birth certificate or applicant's statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fee is required for an age-based petition (37 CFR 1.102(c)). Include adequate evidence of age with the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental quality petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord 'special' status to patent applications for inventions that materially enhance the quality of the environment by contributing to restoration or maintenance of air, water, or soil; petitions should explain how the invention contributes to these elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fee is required. Petitions should be accompanied by statements under 37 CFR 1.102 by the applicant, assignee, or registered attorney/agent explaining the contribution. Applicants desiring to participate should petition that their applications be accorded special status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy-related petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord 'special' status to applications for inventions that materially contribute to (A) discovery/development of energy resources (e.g., fossil fuels, hydrogen, nuclear, solar) or (B) more efficient utilization and conservation of energy resources (e.g., reduced energy consumption in systems/appliances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions should explain how the invention materially contributes to category (A) or (B). No fee is required (37 CFR 1.102(c)). Examples are provided in the guidance to illustrate categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recombinant DNA (safety) special-status petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord special status to applications relating to safety of research in the field of recombinant DNA; petitioners must file an appropriate petition and pay the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions should include statements under 37 CFR 1.102 explaining the relationship of the invention to safety of recombinant DNA research. Fee required. The MPEP references NIH guidelines and emphasizes exceptional importance and desirability of prompt disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination prerequisites (Special Examining Procedure VIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new application may be granted special (accelerated) status only if the applicant complies with each of these items: (A) petition to make special with fee (1.17(h)); (B) presents all claims directed to a single invention or makes an election without traverse; (C) submits a statement that a pre-examination search was made listing field of search by class/subclass and other sources; (D) submits one copy each of the references deemed most closely related if not already of record; (E) submits a detailed discussion of the references pointing out, with the particularity required by 37 CFR 1.111(b) and (c), how the claimed subject matter is patentable over the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a request fails to meet these prerequisites the application remains a new application in its regular turn. Applicant will be given one opportunity to perfect a defective request; discretion applies to further renewals. Divisional applications do not automatically inherit special status; each must meet requirements on its own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination prosecution procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If special accelerated status is granted, the application will be taken up before most other categories (except allowance-ready or time-limited cases) and the examiner will give a complete first action including all essential matters of merit; a first action rejection sets a 3-month shortened period for reply. Applicant encouraged to arrange an interview during the 3-month reply; submit proposed amendment at least one working day before interview (not part of file). After interview or reply, applicant files a 'record' reply restricted to the rejections/objections/requirements; amendments broadening the search are improper. The examiner will, within 1 month from receipt of the formal reply, take up the application for final disposition (final action or notice of allowance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record reply must be limited to issues raised; amendments that require broadening the search will be treated as improper. Examiner's reply to post-final amendments should be prompt (e.g., PTOL-303, pass to issue, or examiner's answer if appeal). Personal interviews after final action not permitted unless requested by examiner; telephonic interviews may be allowed for minor matters. After allowance, accelerated applications get top priority for printing. Failure to comply with procedural restrictions can lead to denial or return to regular status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superconductivity special status
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord 'special' status to patent applications involving superconductivity upon request; requests should be accompanied by a statement under 37 CFR 1.102 that the invention involves superconductive materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fee required. Applicants desiring participation should request special status and include the required statement. Examples of eligible inventions include materials directed to superconductive materials and their manufacture/application.

rubrics_metrics.name: HIV/AIDS and cancer special status
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord 'special' status to patent applications relating to HIV/AIDS and cancer; applicants desiring special status should file a petition and the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) and include a statement explaining how the invention contributes to diagnosis, treatment, or prevention of HIV/AIDS or cancer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must state the contribution; fee is required under 1.17(h). The policy reflects importance and desirability of prompt disclosure in these fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-terrorism inventions special status
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord 'special' status to applications relating to inventions for countering terrorism; applicants should file a petition with the petition fee and a statement explaining how the invention contributes to countering terrorism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include technologies for detecting explosives, aircraft sensors/security systems, vehicular barricades/disabling systems. The guidance cites 18 U.S.C. 2331 definition of international terrorism and indicates that eligible technologies are not limited to listed examples. Fee required (37 CFR 1.17(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biotechnology small-entity special status
rubrics_metrics.description: Small-entity applicants may request special status for biotechnology applications by filing a petition with the petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(h)) and must (A) state or establish small entity status, (B) state that the patent application subject is a major asset of the small entity, and (C) state that development will be significantly impaired if examination is delayed, with an explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must include the required statements and fee. The Office evaluates these assertions; special status is not automatic without meeting these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements of petition to make special
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to make special should be in writing and identify the application by application number and filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet formal requirements may result in the petition not being processed or the application being taken up in its regular turn. Include clear identification to enable correct file entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and recording of petitions to make special
rubrics_metrics.description: Each petition to make special, regardless of grounds or decision, is made of record in the application file along with the decision. The ruling part of the Office must properly enter the petition and decision in the file record; the petition (with attachments) gets a single paper number and the decision a separate paper number in the 'Contents'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support staff in the TC must ensure all prior papers are entered/listed before forwarding for petition consideration. Petitions are decided by the Special Program Examiner of the assigned TC. Proper file management is required to ensure petitions and decisions are traceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of special status once granted
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to diligent prosecution by the applicant, an application once made special and advanced out of turn by reason of a ruling will continue to be special throughout its entire course of prosecution in the USPTO, including appeal to the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no provision for 'withdrawal' from special status; applicants must prosecute diligently to retain the benefits. Transfers between examiners/art units should treat the application as special.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of action (37 CFR 1.103) — general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may suspend action for cause on request of the applicant or on its own initiative under circumstances in 37 CFR 1.103 (including suspension for public safety/defense, statutory invention registration, and requests tied to CPA/RCE/deferral). Suspension applies to impending Office action by the examiner; action cannot be suspended if an applicant reply to an Office action is outstanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension reduces patent term adjustment accumulated (if any) by the number of days of suspension. The Office will notify applicant if it suspends action on its own initiative. Suspension is distinct from extension of time for reply (37 CFR 1.136).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition under 37 CFR 1.103(a) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for suspension under 37 CFR 1.103(a) must be presented as a separate paper, be accompanied by the petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(h)), request a specific and reasonable suspension period not greater than 6 months, and present good and sufficient reasons why suspension is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements are not met, the application will be taken up for action. A petition to suspend to allow submission of an IDS will be denied as failing to present good and sufficient reasons (37 CFR 1.97 provides recourse). Form paragraphs are provided in the MPEP for grant/denial notices. Only the TC Director can grant second or subsequent suspensions; such approval must appear on the Office letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for suspension under 37 CFR 1.103(b)/(c) (CPA/RCE) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for suspension under 1.103(b) or (c) (for CPA or RCE) must be filed at the time of filing the CPA or RCE, specify a suspension period in whole months (maximum 3 months), and include the processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)). If filed with an RCE, the RCE must comply with 1.114 (be accompanied by a submission and the RCE fee). If filed with a CPA, a filing date must be assigned to the CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request is filed but the CPA/RCE is improper (no filing date, missing submission/fee), the Office will not recognize the request for suspension and will send a notice of improper filing; the time period in the prior Office communication continues to run. If the CPA is assigned a filing date despite missing parts, the suspension request will be processed but applicant will be given time to pay missing fees to avoid abandonment. An improper or untimely request (or missing processing fee) will cause action not to be suspended and the application to be placed on the examiner's docket; the applicant will be notified in the next Office communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of examination under 37 CFR 1.103(d) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for deferral of examination may be granted for up to three years from the earliest filing date for which benefit is claimed, provided: (1) the application is an original utility or plant application under 1.53(b) or a national-stage entry after compliance with 1.495; (2) applicant has not filed a nonpublication request under 1.213(a) (or has rescinded under 1.213(b)); (3) the application is in condition for publication as provided in 1.211(c); and (4) the Office has not issued an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151. The request must include the publication fee (1.18(d)) and processing fee (1.17(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may consider deferral when they want to delay examination; requests that do not meet conditions will be denied. Deferral requests cause patent term adjustment reduction for the suspension period. The maximum deferral period is three years from the earliest claimed filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension for public safety or defense (37 CFR 1.103(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may suspend action by order of the Commissioner if: (1) the application is owned by the United States; (2) publication of the invention may be detrimental to public safety or defense; and (3) the appropriate department or agency requests such suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This suspension is instituted on the Office's initiative upon appropriate agency request; applicant will be notified if action is suspended. It is distinct from applicant-requested suspensions and may have national security implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension due to statutory invention registration request
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will suspend action for the entire pendency of an application if the Office has accepted a request to publish a statutory invention registration in the application, except for purposes relating to patent interference proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This suspension lasts the entire pendency for the statutory invention registration; the exception relates to interference proceedings under Subpart E.
